Priority decisions for the project team

Down Bailey · carpet: 8-week lead after payment

Payment not confirmed.

Superior · 36 double-door assemblies; 4-week reported lead

Quoted installation: normally starts 1–2 weeks after actual product delivery. June 12 estimate is past stated validity. OPEN RFI: Relats 20-minute S-label schedule versus Superior 90-minute quote.

Sciens · ceiling sprinkler interface

Basement first (~2–3 planning weeks) followed by residential floors (~1 floor/week planning). Hallway walls need not be reopened, per current field coordination. Fire alarm devices generally reuse locations; patching expected minimal.

Separate unmodeled gates: smoke control / damper work, Fire Alarm permit/integration/testing, door rated assembly inspections, City/AHJ acceptance, painting and resident logistics. These can delay true hallway turnover despite a green 3D ribbon.

Board briefing · six key questions

Which decisions this simulation can and cannot support

1. Floor order: Proposed numeric progression Floor 2 → 21 → PH, grouped by demolition capacity. A true owner notice requires a confirmed active-floor map.
2. Remediation stages: Half-corridor demo → cleanup/remediation → AirMD PRV → wall rebuild / City approval → safe temporary floor condition. Carpet removal is separately authorized, not already included in base SERVPRO scope.
3. Sprinklers + fire doors: Illustrative basement lead in, residential ceiling sequence, then door installation; verify frames and blocking BEFORE drywall closes.
4. Decoration: Only after wall safety approval and the applicable damaging overhead trade operations.
5. New carpet: Eight weeks after Down Bailey actually receives required payment, then floor-by-floor installation after doors and final prep.
6. Overall completion: Not forecastable until alarms, smoke control, inspection durations, materials, permits and commissioning are committed. This simulation does not assert completed work or a contract end date.
